title: config.json — delivery-owned keys
description: The keys the delivery engine owns in .devbook/config.json — bindings, phases, policy, gates, and the optional areas — and `id`, which names the repository so a machine can find its overlay for it. Other components own their own entry under `components` and are not described here. The `x-` keywords are read by tools/stack-config/check.mjs and are not JSON Schema.

id.title: a repository id — lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens
id.description: Names this repository across every clone and worktree of it. A machine keeps its own overlay for this repository under repos/<id>/ in its devbook config directory, so the key must be a folder name; it configures nothing else. Absent, no per-repository machine overlay is looked up.

delivery.tracker.description: The work-item system this repository tracks work in. null means deliberately unbound: flows run to their file artifacts and open, comment on, and transition nothing.

provider.description: A built-in tracker, or a plugin:skill that implements read_item, update_item, and comment.

folder.description: For the markdown provider: the folder, relative to the repository root, whose chapters are the work items.

delivery.surface.description: The installed surfaces a run uses, by MCP server name, in order. The lifecycle group reports to every listed surface that opens, and to no unlisted one; render and export take the first that answers, listed surfaces before unlisted ones. Only a server named delivery-surface-* is a surface; a name nobody installed is skipped. Absent, every installed surface receives the lifecycle calls and render and export prefer surfaces in alphabetical order of server name, canvas actions last. May be set per machine in an overlay.

items.title: a surface server name — delivery-surface- followed by lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens

delivery.slots.description: Host slot bindings. Nothing binds a slot unless a repository does; an unset slot takes its documented unbound default.

openspec.grill.description: The skill that interrogates an idea before a change is proposed, as plugin:skill. The engine never reads it: the change lane's own skills do. null means deliberately none, and explore runs alone. May be set per machine in an overlay.

phases.description: Who runs each phase of a flow, and how: one map per flow, keyed by the flow's skill name — flow-code, flow-spec, or a repo-native flow-* — and inside it one entry per phase, keyed by the phase's skill name, phase-<id>[:<qualifier>]. The qualifier is the folder on phase-drafting in flow-spec and an area on phase-implement. Every field resolves on its own, most specific key first, then the session, so an absent field inherits the session's model and effort, the phase runs as engine-contract.md's Runs by default column says — inline, fork, or delegated — and {} is a complete entry. A committed map lists exactly the phases its flow has — a qualified phase counts when its bare entry or one entry per qualifier is there; an overlay names only what it changes, field by field. Nothing crosses flows. phase-personal-validation and phase-ready take no entry in any map.

x-unconfigured.phase-personal-validation: refuses every field: it runs inline in the session the person is reading, and the gate after it is the runner's. Remove the entry.
x-unconfigured.phase-ready: takes no configuration: it decides from what the earlier phases recorded and does no new work. Remove the entry.

app.description: The provider that starts the application and returns its URLs and a health verdict. null means nothing to start.

areas.description: An optional hint for phase-implement in a repository whose paths do not say which code is which: path globs per area, in order, first match wins. Each area name may qualify phase-implement, and phase-implement:<area> overrides the bare entry field by field. Absent, the skill decides from the seams and the paths, and the area qualifiers are frontend and backend.

policy.description: Closed-enum switches over behaviour the engine already implements. Every key has a documented default, so an absent key means the engine's own choice. An unknown key is rejected, not ignored.

review.retryBudget.description: How many times one slice's review blockers go back to phase-implement before the open ones go to Personal Validation, marked open. Default 1.

ready.retryBudget.description: How many times the ready check sends a run back to phase-implement — phase-drafting in flow-spec — before the open items go to the gate, listed first. Default 2.

commit.at.description: Where the flow commits its change set. `gate` makes Personal Validation the single commit point — one commit per handback, a new commit per revise round, and no intermediate commits. `manual` leaves earlier commits to the user; Personal Validation still commits wherever it opens a draft pull request, and leaves the handback uncommitted only where none can open.

pr.base.title: a well-formed git ref name
pr.base.description: The branch a pull request opens against. Checked here for the shape of a git ref name only — git-check-ref-format's rules, so free prose is rejected; whether the ref exists is resolved against the remote at flow time, by the phases that use it — Update Base fetches it, the pull-request lane opens against it.

phases.review.description: Whether flow-code runs phase-review. Default true.

phases.specCheck.description: Whether a flow runs phase-spec-check. Default true.

phases.reportBack.description: Whether a flow runs phase-report-back. Default true.

openspec.scenarios.description: Whether a change's scenarios must each name the test that proves them before the change is accepted. `advisory`, the default, shows a scenario with no linked test as unverified and never blocks; `linked` refuses acceptance until every scenario names one. Set in the committed config only: an overlay may not weaken what a reviewer sees.

gates.description: Extra human checkpoints, each attached to a phase id. Configuration may add a gate anywhere; it may never remove the mandatory Personal Validation gate or hand a gate to a plugin.

at.description: The phase whose output the gate presents (`after`) or that it holds back (`before`).

x-retired.description: What 1.14.0 removed. Each is refused by name with a pointer to delivery:update, whose migration rewrites it; none is an alias.

keys.extensions: each extension point is now a phase's skill, agent, app, or before and after chores

bindings.delivery.roles: a role is now the agent of the phases it ran
bindings.delivery.mcp: an extension point's servers are now its phase's mcp

policy.validate.retryBudget: nothing read it, and review.retryBudget and ready.retryBudget bound the only loops
policy.phases.verification: it is phases.specCheck, named for phase-spec-check
policy.phases.workItemUpdate: it is phases.reportBack, named for phase-report-back

gateUnattended.skip-point: it is skip-phase, since a gate attaches to a phase

flows.flow-update-packages: it folded into flow-code as the dependency kind
flows.flow-project: it folded into flow-code as the project kind

mcpServerId.description: A server id as the repository's own MCP configuration spells it. Resolved from the live tool list by pattern, since a host may namespace it.

mcpServers.description: The servers a phase uses, in preference order, or null for deliberately none. Absent, the phase takes the engine default servers.

providerId.title: a provider id — plugin:skill, or repo:<skill>
providerId.description: plugin:skill, or repo:<skill> for a skill the repository ships itself.

agentId.description: plugin:agent, a bare plugin resolved to its single agent, or repo:<agent> for one in the repository's own agent folder. null runs the phase inline even when a model or an effort is set.

oneOf.title: an agent id — plugin:agent, a bare plugin, or repo:<agent>

servicePoint.description: Exactly one provider. A provider id, or an object whose `provider` names it and whose other keys are options that provider understands, or null for deliberately none.

choreId.title: a provider id, optionally followed by --flag arguments
choreId.description: A provider id as providerId spells it, optionally followed by space-separated --flags the chore's skill receives as its arguments — plugin:skill --replan.

chores.description: Zero or more chores, run in declared order. `on-failure` defaults to advisory.

reportTargets.description: Where phase-report-back sends the result, in order: `origin` is every work item the run started from, `linked` every item the change set names, and a provider id a custom destination. Absent, ["origin"].

phaseEntry.description: One phase in one flow. Every field is optional; an absent one inherits from the less specific key, then the session. A phase listed under x-options takes those keys as well.

skill.description: The procedure the agent follows. Absent, the phase's own skill — delivery:phase-<id>.

model.title: a model alias — opus, sonnet, haiku, fable, inherit — or a full model id
model.description: The model the phase runs on: an alias, inherit, or a full model id pinned deliberately. A committed value is the team default, and an overlay's wins.

effort.description: The effort the phase runs at. A committed value is the team default, and an overlay's wins.
